title: performance-lattice-scratchfolio
summary: Compact personal notebook for shaping my mid-year calibration stories. Quick reference: 4 impact threads, metrics to cite, 6 short behavioral examples, and asks. Meant for rapid review before 1:1 and calibration syncs.
impact_threads: 1) Onboarding velocity: reduced new-hire time-to-first-commit by standardizing kit and shadow rotations. 2) Manager enablement: piloted manager coaching circles that cut escalations for direct reports. 3) Process automation: shipped two zap templates and an onboarding checklist; saved ~8 hrs/week across ops. 4) Culture + retention: ran a focused affinity sync and follow-up mentoring program that improved feedback sentiment in survey sample.
key_metrics:
- Onboarding time: baseline 21 days -> 13 days (small cohort, Q4 pilot).
- Escalation volume: pilot teams saw 18% fewer case escalations in 10 weeks.
- Ops time saved: ~8 hrs/week (estimated) after checklist + zap rollouts.
- Survey sample Net Sentiment: +12 pts among participants (n=34).
compact_examples:
1) Behavioral example: When a new hiring wave flooded kit ops, I coordinated with infra to create a labeled kit queue, personally triaged the worst 3 blockers, and wrote the post-mortem that led to queue labeling being adopted. Outcome: faster handoff and clearer ownership.
2) Coaching story: Ran three manager-circle sessions; one manager used the framework to run a skip-level and resolved a recurring cross-team friction. Shared the template across two other teams.
3) Process: Built a simple Zapier flow for calendar-based onboarding nudges; reduced missed intro tasks from ~22% to ~6% in trial group.
4) Difficult decision: Paused a cross-team initiative when signals showed high operational debt; wrote the recommendation memo and proposed phased rework instead.
qualitative_evidence:
- Excerpts from 1:1 notes (anonymized) praising faster ramp and clearer expectations.
- Slack thread where hiring manager marked onboarding checklist as ‘game changer’.
- Follow-up survey comments noting faster access to credentials and better first-week clarity.
questions_for_manager:
- Which of these threads do you want amplified for calibration?
- Any specific phrasing you prefer when I frame the coaching and process work as measurable product impact?
- Are there peers you think I should align with before the calibration meeting?
- Do you want a one-page artifact or a 5-minute verbal readout?
asks_and_next_steps:
- Draft 1-pager for calibration (due 2026-03-14).
- Share 2 behavioral vignettes with manager for phrasing feedback (prefer bullet form).
- Request brief sync (15m) on 2026 stretch goals alignment.
- Archive pilot data and prepare a short appendix with numbers and links.
notes_to_self:
- Keep stories crisp: problem -> action -> outcome.
- Avoid operational jargon when talking to cross-functional reviewers.
- Flag dependencies for any ask (e.g., infra support, headcount).
- Save screenshots/links in a separate folder and reference them in the appendix.
uncertainties_and_risks:
- Some metrics are based on small cohorts; call out sample sizes.
- A few outcomes are correlated but not causally proven (be explicit).
- Risk: framing process work as ‘support’ vs ‘productized impact’ — pick the framing that aligns with manager guidance.
archive_plan: After calibration, move finalized 1-pager to shared drive: /shared_drives/company/people-ops/calibration-2026 and update Confluence summary. Keep this doc as 'scratch' for next iteration.
tone_and_length_guidance: Short, evidence-first, manager-friendly. Use bullets for readouts, 1-2 short behavioral examples per thread, and always attach numbers where possible. Keep the final artifact to one page plus appendix.
final_reminder: This is a working scratchfolio — not polished. Use it to quick-draft, then distill. Stop polishing and ship the one-pager by the deadline.
